subject: English
central_question: How do poverty, migration, child labour and inherited social systems steal childhood while a few children still try to imagine a different future?
in_scope_units: About Anees Jung and the focus on exploited children.
Saheb’s migration from Dhaka, rag-picking, lack of schooling and broken promises.
Bare feet, Seemapuri, garbage as survival and wonder, tennis and the tea-stall job.
Hazards of glass furnaces, caste, custom, middlemen and the loss of initiative.
Comprehension, figures of speech, paradox, note-making and report-writing tasks.
banned_topics: A general history of Bangladesh or Delhi not provided in the chapter.
Technical details of glass manufacture beyond the conditions described in Firozabad.

known_pitfalls.claim: Garbage has the same meaning for children and adults.
known_pitfalls.correction: For elders it is survival; for children it also contains wonder and hope of finding a coin.

known_pitfalls.claim: Saheb becomes happier after paid work.
known_pitfalls.correction: His carefree look disappears and the canister symbolises service under an owner.

known_pitfalls.claim: Mukesh has already escaped the industry.
known_pitfalls.correction: He has only expressed a determined dream and willingness to walk to a garage.

known_pitfalls.claim: Workers remain poor because they do not work hard.
known_pitfalls.correction: The text identifies caste, debt, middlemen, police, bureaucracy, politics and exhausted initiative.

recommended_example_progression: Use Think as you read Q1 to introduce Saheb’s search and migration.
Use Q2 to analyse barefoot children and poverty.
Use Q3 to contrast rag-picking with tea-stall employment.
Use the Firozabad questions for hazards and Mukesh’s attitude.
Use Understanding the text Q3 and Thinking about language for systemic exploitation and style.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Understanding the text Questions 1–3, Talking about the text, Thinking about language and Things to do/report-writing activities.
